conviction_note: The Q4 guide is the line. Enphase's own numbers show the 2026 5%-method safe-harbor book ($202.4m) almost fully recognised by the end of Q3 (34.5 + 84.3 + ~75 guided = ~$194m), and the July 4, 2026 begin-construction deadline has passed, so Q4 loses ~$75m of revenue that a ~$305m Q4 consensus (one undated Benzinga snapshot) may not fully reflect. US counterparties (SolarEdge, Sunrun, WoodMac) also point down. Against that: 21.9% of float short at 5.5-5.9 days to cover, a +28.7 vol-point put skew, the stock down ~22% since the July print, and a +38.6% squeeze in Feb 2026. That leaves a modest bearish lean (p_up 44) on a large move (abs 12), so the scaled number is -1.44. The findings sum to -0.9 because the positioning and Europe offsets are sized on their own.
bar: Q3 2026: company guide of $290-320m revenue (midpoint $305m; ~$75m safe harbor; 130-150 MWh batteries; GAAP GM 42-45%, non-GAAP 44-47%; 'more than 70% booked to midpoint'), per the Q2 release coverage https://mercomindia.com/enphase-revenue-falls-20-yoy-readies-next-generation-storage-products and https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/enphase-energy-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-28/. Street: revenue $303.7m and non-GAAP EPS $0.47 (whisper $0.45) per https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/ENPH; a Benzinga snapshot gives Q3 ~$305m and Q4 2026 revenue ~$304.6-306.1m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/ENPH/earnings-forecasts, undated snapshot). The Q3 revenue bar is sourced to the company guide and two estimate sources. The Q4 bar rests on one undated aggregator, so the guidance finding is capped. EPS bars disagree: Northland/MarketBeat cite $0.18-0.19, which looks GAAP; Earnings Whispers gives $0.47 non-GAAP.
positioning_check: Short interest 21.9% of float, 5.5-5.9 days to cover, as of the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://tapeboard.com/stock/ENPH, read 2026-10-27); up from 17.5% of float and 4.6 days on 2026-08-20 (https://equibles.com/stocks/enph/shortinterest). So this is a crowded short that kept building into the print. Baseline: 25-delta skew +28.72 vol points (downside heavily paid), ATM IV 144%, event-implied move 11.48% (straddle 12.08%), put/call OI 1.0, spot $31.79, 56% below the 52-week high, 5-day -1.37%, 20-day -0.13%; Earnings Whispers shows -21.9% since the July 28 print. Squeeze precedent: +38.6% on the 2026-02-03 print. Reaction history is 7 down out of 8, median |move| 11.62%.

findings.finding: Enphase's own disclosure shows $202.4m of 2026 safe-harbor agreements under the 5% ITC method, against ~$194m already recognised or guided (Q1 $34.5m + Q2 $84.3m + ~$75m in the Q3 guide). The $878.6m Physical Work Test book is not expected to produce revenue until 2028, and the July 4, 2026 begin-construction deadline has passed. So Q4 2026 should lose most of the ~$75m Q3 safe-harbor contribution. On ~$230m of Q3 core revenue, a Q4 guide near the ~$305m Q4 consensus needs about $75m of offset from Europe, the G5 battery launch or US recovery, which management has not described.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same setup a year ago: Q3 2025 was flattered by $70.9m of safe-harbor revenue, and the Q4 2025 guide implied a ~$80m sequential drop (Susquehanna, 2025-10-30, https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/enphase-energy-price-target-lowered-to-33-from-37-at-susquehanna-thefly). The stock fell 15.15% (baseline, 2025-10-28). The Feb 2026 guide surprise went the other way, +38.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 consensus snapshot (~$305m, Benzinga) is flat on Q3 and does not show a step-down. If the cliff were fully priced, Q4 estimates would sit near $250m and the analysts' Q4 EPS would be below Q3. Northland's Q4 EPS of $0.27 is above its Q3 $0.18 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/northland-securities-forecasts-enphase-energy-q3-earnings-2026-08-06/, page no longer shows it). Partly priced: the stock is down 22% since July and the skew is put-heavy. Capped because the Q4 bar is one undated source and the short is crowded.
findings.independence: The July 4, 2026 begin-construction deadline and the 5% method's limits are documented separately at https://www.solarpermitsolutions.com/blog/solar-tax-credits-2026-what-changed-after-obbba. The safe-harbor amounts all come from one company document (the Q2 release and call).

findings.finding: Counterparties that spoke after Enphase's July 28 guide all point to softer US residential demand than Enphase's 'US-led +10% Q3 sell-through'. SolarEdge (Aug 5) said it does not expect the usual US Q3 residential rebound and guided Q3 to $310-340m against $375m consensus. Sunrun (Aug 5) reported Q2 subscriber additions down 31% y/y and cut its 2026 cash-generation guide to $200-375m from $250-450m. Wood Mackenzie/SEIA see H2 2026 US residential interconnections at 1.6 GW against 2.1 GW in H1, after Q2 at 995 MW, a five-year low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ENPH has fallen on 7 of its last 8 prints, with -14 to -16% on three 2025 prints where US demand commentary disappointed (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer and industry series, not Enphase's own numbers, and they are three months old. The 22% slide since July likely absorbed much of the SolarEdge read-through (SEDG -24% that day). The unpriced part is the Q4 seasonal step-down implied by WoodMac's H2 figure, which the flat ~$305m Q4 consensus does not show. Enphase is US 78% of revenue, so this is net of Europe's 22% (see the Europe finding).
findings.independence: Sunrun Q2 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001469367/000162828026053349/exhibit991q226.htm; Wood Mackenzie/SEIA via https://mercomindia.com/us-solar-installations-jump-45-yoy-to-11-4-gw-in-q2-2026. These are three independent sources, but all are proxies for Enphase sell-through.

findings.finding: Europe (22% of Q2 revenue; revenue +35% q/q and sell-through +30% in Q2) has a dated Q4 demand driver: the Netherlands ends net metering at the end of 2026, a cited battery-attach driver (Dutch battery activations +102% q/q). The IQ Battery G5, at ~40% lower cost per kWh, starts shipping in Q4 2026. Both could partly offset the safe-harbor cliff in the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: European strength has not protected the stock: Europe grew in Q2 and the stock still fell 3.44% on the July print (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Management guided Q3 Europe flat on seasonality, so the Q4 Dutch pull-in has not been quantified anywhere. If it were priced, the Q4 consensus would be built on Europe growth rather than safe harbor. The 22% revenue share limits the size.
findings.independence: SolarEdge also cited strong European demand in Q2 (https://www.pv-tech.org/solaredge-forecasts-weaker-q3-despite-20-q2-revenue-growth/). G5 timing per https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/enphase-energy-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-28/.

findings.finding: Short interest rose to 21.9% of float with 5.5-5.9 days to cover (Sept 30 settlement), from 17.5% and 4.6 days in August, while the 25-delta skew sits at +28.7 vol points. The stock already squeezed +38.6% on the Feb 2026 print when the guide beat a bearish bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one up-move in eight was +38.6% (2026-02-03), on a guide that beat a depressed bar with heavy short interest.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-30 (settlement as shown on the page, read 2026-10-27)
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is public, but it skews the payoff. Any Q4 guide that is merely 'not as bad' as the safe-harbor math forces covering from 5-6 days of volume. That asymmetry is not in a put-heavy skew that pays for downside.
findings.independence: Equibles short interest series, 2026-08-20: 17.5% of float, 4.6 days (https://equibles.com/stocks/enph/shortinterest).

findings.finding: Tesla's Q3 2026 storage deployments were 13.7 GWh against a company-compiled consensus of 15.9 GWh, and storage revenue fell 16% y/y. This is a weak read on home-storage pricing and demand. Powerwall is not broken out, and most of the figure is utility Megapack.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of ENPH reacting to Tesla storage prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and only loosely tied to residential, so it is sized near zero.

outside_window.finding: The Physical Work Test safe-harbor book ($878.6m) is expected to start producing revenue only in 2028, and the IQ Vault 80 commercial battery ships from Q1 2027. Neither lands inside this window except as possible commentary in the guide.

baseline_tension: The negative lean agrees with the +28.7 put skew and the 7-of-8 down history, so much of it is plausibly priced. A 21.9% short interest and the Feb +38.6% squeeze cut against it, which keeps p_up near 50 despite the safe-harbor arithmetic.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short: 21.9% of float, 5.5-5.9 days to cover) and rule 6 (Q4 bar is one undated aggregator snapshot) cut the safe-harbor cliff guidance finding from -3.0 to -2.0. Both were applied once, as a single shrink.
Rule 7 cut the US counterparty demand finding from -1.5 to -1.2 because of the crowded short.
p_up moved from 42 to 44 for the crowded short and the unsourced Q4 bar; abs_move_pct stays 12 (rule 8 / core: uncertainty never shrinks it).
